steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: All is prepared. Come Matins, the people will take... take their final communion.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Will your strings... lament for me? Or will they celebrate me?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I am clueless about music, Arturia. Just as I cannot understand you.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Here you stand, and here I empathize with you, yet you seem a total blank.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I am no more than free to perform according to Your Excellency's will. My music is but a mirror.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: A mirror... hah.
The elderly abbot lifts a porcelain tray, his hands quivering amidst string's overtones.
He appears as if wrestling with the sound that echoes throughout the dark, awaiting their end.
He was still young when the sounds of paradise arose in the abbey years and years ago, so young that his reflection in the fountain did not yet show a single hair of white.

Wild fowls were drawn to these roving soils, fluttering through skies rich with organ chords, flying for the square. In his old age, the last abbot handed the monastery down to him, Cleric Stefano, the youngest of them all.

a.text: 'You must be their keeper, that they live in Paradise.'
And how? How would I see them stay in Paradise?

steps.text: Abbot Torregrossa shuts his eyes. Storied is his life.
The strings continue to echo, echo, echo. And then—
He lets his hands go.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How painful. So this is your choice.
From behind the sealed chapel entrance comes the muffled sound of speech.
Federico stands in the spacious hall for a while, listening, then turns to walk upstairs.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Equipment normal.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The only loss has been one communicator.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Current objective remains unchanged. Proceeding with mission.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Locked onto suspect.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: How're things in there?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Communion should be over by now.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Is it as bad in there as I think?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Signs point to yes.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Damn. How's Federico?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Unreachable.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The Church of the Deep doesn't breed pushovers for monsters. Does he know that?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Someone needs to do the work. Status on Lemuen and Serpilia?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: They got your message and went underground to investigate.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Alright. That means the trickiest job of all is all ours.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Let's open up.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: And be where we may, and face what we may, it remains that we must respect each other in kind, care for each other in kind—

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: —Good morning, emissaries of the Holy City.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The trays are empty.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Richele, get every inhabitant under control. I'll handle the abbot.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Is there something amiss, emissary?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Amiss? Well, here's the thing... what's got you so down, Most Reverend Abbot? So insistent that Matins today has to be the 'final' one?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'm pretty sure Lemuen's informed you that after you dock back up with Laterano, there's a real chance you'll continue serving as this monastery's abbot...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Emissaries of Laterano, you question me... but on what basis?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I have made my choice—renounced my vain hopes that all could be met with equal salvation.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The monastery's course is run. On this final Matins, may all our trays be empty.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I have just delivered them the news. The Sanctilaminium Ambrosii has agreed to return to Laterano.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Return to Laterano...?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Sir, don't tell me you thought we'd let the Church of the Deep off the hook...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: ...I told you, my choice is made.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Oren, he's telling the truth.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The inhabitants haven't shown any signs of change. I've examined the trays, and they're clean.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Yes. I prepared the flesh of those monsters by my own hand, and mixed it all into the bread.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But though it was meant for Matins, I locked it away in a cabinet underground, lest my starving people ingest it accidentally.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Now that Aulus has left, that which you fear flourishes no longer.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: This is the key to the cabinet door. Take it, it is my plea. This will prove that what I say is true. Perhaps you will know better how handle the Church of the Deep's givings.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Thank you for cooperating.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Looks like my gun's resting easy today...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What, are you sad about that?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Come again?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: No, I'm just breathing out, finally. We got the rough part over with. Work should be getting back on track now... right?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Lemuen, catch what the abbot said? I'm bringing the key down now.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You don't have to.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Someone smashed the cabinet open. It's empty inside.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yellowing napkins, pottery shards all over the floor. All the details line up with the abbot's description.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: And looking at previous accounts, the consequences of eating this stuff are irreversible... If he'd made them partake already, he wouldn't need to lie to us anymore.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Which means someone's gone and thieved this little 'Eucharist.'

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We have to find them immediately.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Uh, finding one person in an abbey this big—maybe a tall order?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's hitting me. I think we've all forgotten a few things.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: For one, Gerald heard about how that Sankta girl fell, and that dealt him a huge shock.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But we would've never let any word out about the falling. How did Gerald learn of it?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: And for another, just what was the deal with that fire in the sacrarium?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Without someone else's encouragement, the abbot might not have been so dogmatic either...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: After all of this, I've got a bad feeling our abbot's not alone in his despair.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: When Fortuna went into the chapel, I remember somebody else was in there.

a.text: So this is the Abbot's choice...
Not that it hasn't crossed my mind before—that things would ultimately turn out this way.
He is kindhearted. So kindhearted that he strove to this day, embracing such lofty ideals, and in turn, he lost to weakness at the very last moment.
But I am not like him.
It was long, long ago that I gave up hope.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh? A guest.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I have to say, I'm a little surprised. I gave you fair warning, but...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I thought with all your rational, logical judgment, you'd conclude that 'there are other matters of higher priority to handle,' or something like that.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How long has it been since we last met, Federico? Five, maybe close to six years?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hm? Aren't you going to say—'Discontinue this meaningless speech, fugitive Arturia?'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Or do you finally plan to switch to a different greeting?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why not go back to those days when you lived with me, then... and call me Soror?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh...? And you're still not angry?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The first instant you came through the door and saw me, you didn't even make a move. That's unlike you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Let me take a guess at why you're so out of sorts, then.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you waiting for something?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Or... are you hesitating?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Listen. Sounds of all kinds fill this little monastery.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Sorrow, pain, suspicion, resentment... and despair.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: All woven together. More exquisitely touching than any man-made melody could ever be.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Ah... how very curious. Federico Giallo, have you felt anything? Is there any note out there that can dance within your brain, the one so different to how normal people think?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Fugitive Arturia, I have fully assessed your words and actions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My present priority to address is not you.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You aren't in the chapel, Senior Federico?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I thought you and your colleagues all had your eyes fixed on the Most Reverend Abbot...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are the prevailing suspect in this series of abnormalities.

spans.text: are the prevailing suspect in this series of abnormalities.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I honor... yes, I honor His Excellency's choice.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: We all respect him. Love him. This was always the way it would be, for we are all under His Excellency's wing...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It's simple to understand, isn't it?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: When every cause sees you expelled from the cities, and your only choice is to roam the wastes, and you've become sure your end lies in death...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: When your stomach groans with hunger, and all you ever find is despair, no matter where you walk, and eternity seems to have you trapped in the land that eats of man...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: That's when past a gentle hill, and over the rock, you enter a canyon.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You see a building past the dust, a building that could dare to be a city, where its people bring you food, and let you stay in a room for the night.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes, there is only meager grit-like bread, and a bowl of watery soup.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes, there are cracks in the walls of the rooms, forever in need of repair...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But you have not died in the wastes. You have been admitted.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And that is why some of you call this place Paradise.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: 'Paradise'... yet it was a sham.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Not long after I arrived here, I found... that a Sarkaz friend of mine who'd caught Oripathy had vanished from my side.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I spent an age searching for her, only to find... she was here all along, in a room in the basement. They say it used to be a training room. Its walls are sturdier than all...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It's to that room where they send the deathly ill.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Improvised protective equipment cannot obstruct the propagation of Originium dust with any effectiveness.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: We didn't have any other way.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Maybe you want to tell me how the sick could decide in their own final moments to leave the monastery, and go out into the wastes alone to wait for death to take them?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: We can only bury this pain out of sight, and cover our ears, and turn not to look... We could never save anybody, and there's no one who could save us.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But even this facade of serenity is waiting to be shattered in the end.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: And here we are. You've come.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Our mission here is to maintain order.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Of course. It wasn't any of you that destroyed our life here, after all. It simply and naturally came to the way it is now, as a matter of course.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: And no matter how carefully I tend to the flowers I plant, when it's time for them to wilt, they will transform in invisible measures until they're beyond recognition. It's all the same.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You have been affected by Arturia.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You mean by Seniora Arturia's music?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Perhaps. In them, I often hear recollections of these things.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But she's never been a part of our lives. I know, she simply takes our distress, our suffering, as ornaments for her leisure...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: And so, how could she ever go far enough to disturb our wills, to make these choices for us?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Dangerous articles detected.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You have concealed a large quantity of flammables beneath this sacrarium—no—this entire monastery.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It was a... possible alternative.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Whether you came or not, the tranquil life of this monastery was never going to last.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Have you seen what hunger and fear of wandering the barrens can drive people to, Senior Federico?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I have.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Before things reach the point of no redemption... I will end it all.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément Dubois, you are a suspect in the destruction of the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii, and are involved in multiple cases that concern or have concerned the rights of Lateran citizens.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You have been confirmed an executorial target by the Notarial Hall. In accordance with regulation, I will immediately proceed to apprehend you.
Federico never gives more warning than needed. The gun in his hands simply serves the place of speech.
Clément has not collapsed.
The wasting man clutches at his arm, where all feeling is lost, and gives a bitter smile.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Destruction of lighter confirmed.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why... won't you kill me?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why go to the bother of aiming for the lighter?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your actions have not directly led to the deaths of any Lateran citizens. The law would not sentence you to death.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The law... So many years I've lived here, hearkening to His Excellency's guidance, following your law.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I feel its bind in ordinary times... Yet in chaos, in the time we need it most, it disappears without a trace.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: There was some point where the music of Seniora Arturia became all I could even hear.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Senior Federico, is it the law of Laterano that wants to save me... or is it you, yourself?
